subject: Availability guarantee packaging — carveouts & discount clarification
messages:
From: Oliver Park <oliver.park@greenleafsys.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify uptime bundle + carveouts

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. To move toward procurement we need a clearer write-up of two things before our next finance review:

1) A concise matrix showing uptime tiers, response windows (P1/P2), and what services are covered by each tier (monitoring, KV-cache warm standby, warm spare capacity).
2) Clear definition of carveouts/excused downtime (scheduled maintenance, planned model swaps, force majeure) and whether those count against uptime SLAs.

Also — our procurement team asked whether you offer a volume-tier discount tied to committed monthly token spend or ARR; if so, what are the breakpoints and whether discounts apply to retainer/on-call fees or just per-token rates.

Can you share a short document and any sample language your legal team would accept for the carveouts? We want to avoid a long redline loop if possible.

Appreciate it,
Oliver
Account Operations
Greenleaf Systems

--
Attachment: procurement_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@greenleafsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-04-30T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime bundle + carveouts

Oliver — thanks for the note.

Quick reply: I attached a compact matrix (uptime_matrix_v1.csv) and a one-page proposal (SLA_Pack_Proposal_v1.pdf) that callers out:
- three uptime tiers (99.5%, 99.9%, 99.99%) with associated P1/P2 response SLAs,
- coverage scope per tier,
- typical escalation windows and retainer approach.

On carveouts: our standard position treats planned maintenance with >=72 hours notice as excused if it impacts <4 hours per quarter. Emergency model swaps (security or critical model patches) are treated as excused for the first 2 maintenance events per year; beyond that we negotiate credits. Force majeure follows the usual legal language, but we can be explicit about rota/on-call expectations.

High level on pricing: we typically offer volume-tier discounts tied to committed ARR or 12-month token commitments — discounts apply to per-token generation rates, not to third-party cloud infrastructure surcharges. Retainer/on-call fees are usually discounted only at enterprise commit breakpoints (example in the PDF).

Looping in Marissa for deal ops and Karthik for pricing optimization. If you can share a target commit horizon (12 vs 36 months) and an expected monthly token profile (burst %), we’ll give you a crisp breakpoint table.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: uptime_matrix_v1.csv, SLA_Pack_Proposal_v1.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@greenleafsys.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-01T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime bundle + carveouts

Oliver — good to meet you in the call yesterday. Short note with what we typically recommend for customers at your scale: 

Proposal summary (preview):
- Baseline commitment: 12-month token commit (committed ARR) with monthly true-ups.
- Breakpoints: Commit >= $150k ARR => 7% off per-token rates; >= $300k ARR => 12% off; >= $600k ARR => 18% off.
- Retainer (on-call) discount: 10% discount on the retainer at >= $300k ARR; waived setup fee at >= $600k ARR.
- Crediting: We push for a simple credit matrix for unplanned downtime; planned maintenance with >=72h notice excluded.

Questions for you: do you expect predictable steady-state token consumption, or heavy seasonality? If seasonality >30% peak/valley we usually structure a buffer clause to avoid large true-up swings.

If those breakpoints look plausible I’ll ask pricing (Karthik) to produce a firm quote and Laura to prep a short carveout clause we can share for initial legal review.

Thanks — Marissa
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Oliver Park <oliver.park@greenleafsys.com>
Date: 2025-05-01T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime bundle + carveouts

Hi all — quick pricing note. I adjusted the breakpoint proposal to reflect unit economics and the operational cost of higher availability: 

Suggested revision: 
- Tiered ARR breakpoints (annualized): $150k => 6% per-token, $350k => 11% per-token + 8% off retainer, $700k => 18% per-token + 15% off retainer.
- For 99.99% uptime we add a modest availability surcharge (applies only to the portion of traffic routed to redundant warm spares).
- Carveouts: we accept planned maintenance >=72h notice as excused. For emergency model swaps, propose explicit limit of 3 excused events/year; credits start at event #4.

Oliver — if you can confirm a ballpark committed ARR we’ll lock the numbers and include a pro forma invoice.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Pricing Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Oliver Park <oliver.park@greenleafsys.com>, Contracts <contracts@greenleafsys.com>
Date: 2025-05-01T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify uptime bundle + carveouts (legal wording)

Oliver / Contracts team — attaching a short redline that narrows the carveouts and removes ambiguous terms. Key points:
- "Planned maintenance" must be documented and scheduled with >=72h notice. Any maintenance that results in >2 hours downtime in a single event will require an operational post-mortem and potential crediting.
- Emergency model swaps (security/critical fixes): allow up to 3 excused events/year; provide notice within 24 hours when possible; events beyond 3 trigger a credit of 0.5% of monthly bill per event (capped at 2% per month).
- We added a definition for "regional failover" to clarify when failover to another region will be considered excused.

See attached: redlines_Greenleaf_20250501.docx

If these are acceptable I can convert into contract language for your counsel to review.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Park <oliver.park@greenleafsys.com>, Contracts <contracts@greenleafsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-05-02T15:43:00-07:00
Subject: Final: Availability bundle + discount carveouts (next steps)

Oliver — thanks for the quick turnaround. Per the internal discussion above, summary of what we’re prepared to put on the table for Greenleaf: 

- Pricing & breakpoints (12-month commitment): $150k ARR => 6% per-token discount; $350k => 11% per-token + 8% retainer discount; $700k => 18% per-token + 15% retainer discount and waived setup.
- Uptime tiers: 99.5 / 99.9 / 99.99 with documented scope in the attached PDF.
- Carveouts: planned maintenance with >=72h notice excluded; emergency model swaps: up to 3 excused events/year (credits start after event #3); force majeure standard language included.
- Availability surcharge: small surcharge for traffic routed to warm-spare redundancy for 99.99% tier (shown in matrix).

Next steps:
1) I’ll upload an initial redline (Laura’s doc) and a commercial SOW to the shared proposal link: https://redwood.app/ds/GLS-3812/proposal
2) If legal is comfortable, we can send a DocuSign for signature. We can also schedule a 30-minute wrap-up call to confirm final commit horizon.

Proposed wrap-up call slots: Tue 2025-05-06 10:00-10:30 PT or Wed 2025-05-07 14:00-14:30 PT. Which works for you?

Oliver — happy to jump on either slot.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
